old_also.name: Festival Face à la Mer
old_also.hook: A small free jazz, blues and world-music festival staged over a few September evenings on the seafront esplanade — literally programmed, as the name says, facing the Mediterranean, with the silhouette of the Îles d'Hyères on the horizon.
old_also.text: A small free jazz, blues and world-music festival staged over a few September evenings on the seafront esplanade — literally programmed, as the name says, facing the Mediterranean, with the silhouette of the Îles d'Hyères on the horizon. The name is the whole idea: the stage looks straight out at the sea, so the horizon is the backdrop. What makes it worth timing a visit around is when it falls — early September, its fourth edition in 2026, once the August crush has drained away and Cavalaire is at its best and quietest. It is the shoulder-season send-off, and it teaches the real rhythm of this coast: the good nights here come after the crowds leave, not during them. Signal 4th edition, early September 2026, Esplanade Sainte-Estelle; free jazz/blues/world evenings; the 3rd edition ran 4–7 Sep 2025 (Ville de Cavalaire + Festivalenfrance listings)

old.name: Les Escales Musicales
old.hook: The town's real summer live-music engine — a free, roving concert series (jazz, soul, funk, pop) that turns the quays, Place des Bains and the squares into open-air stages through the season.
old.text: The town's real summer live-music engine — a free, roving concert series (jazz, soul, funk, pop) that turns the quays, Place des Bains and the squares into open-air stages through the season. This is how a modest town does live music: not a fixed venue but a municipal series that moves, night to night, from the port to the squares — the actual answer to 'where's the live spot?' is 'wherever the Escale is this week.' It is the honest heart of Cavalaire's evening: free, outdoor, family-easy, and unmistakably seasonal, running only July into early September (it closes 1 Sept 2026 with PashGang on the Esplanade Sainte-Estelle). The bigger names — Hélène Ségara on 23 July, Julie Zenatti on 12 August — play the Sainte-Estelle esplanade the same summer, and those are free too; but the terroir-true thing is the roving programme on the quays. Signal Free itinerant concerts, Thu 2 Jul 2026 (The Color Gipsy, Place des Bains, 18:00) through 1 Sep (PashGang, Esplanade Sainte-Estelle); listed by the Ville de Cavalaire and Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme

old.label: Ramatuelle

old.name: Gassin
old.label: ~25 min
old.hook: A medieval village stacked at 200 m with bougainvillea-hung facades and the Androuno, at ~29 cm reputed to be one of the narrowest streets in the world.
old.text: A medieval village stacked at 200 m with bougainvillea-hung facades and the Androuno, at ~29 cm reputed to be one of the narrowest streets in the world. Classed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France; its ridge gives a full 360° sweep over the gulf, the Îles d'Or and, on clear days, the Alps — the peninsula's best free panorama.

old_also.name: Gassin
old_also.hook: A medieval hill-village ringed by a rampart-walk terrace — the Promenade/Place deï Barri — shaded by centuries-old hackberry trees, with restaurant balconies hanging over the whole gulf. Best at dusk, when the day-trippers thin.
old_also.text: A medieval hill-village ringed by a rampart-walk terrace — the Promenade/Place deï Barri — shaded by centuries-old hackberry trees, with restaurant balconies hanging over the whole gulf. Best at dusk, when the day-trippers thin. Officially one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, Gassin sits some 200 m up with a commanding read of the coast — its founders built high precisely to see sea-raiders coming, and that defensive height is now the finest free viewpoint around: in one slow turn you take in the Bay of Saint-Tropez, the dark Massif des Maures and the Golden Isles. The oddity to hunt for: l'Androuno, a lane just 29 cm wide, claimed among the narrowest streets in the world. Signal Verified: classed Plus Beaux Villages de France, ~200 m elevation, Place/Promenade deï Barri panorama over the bay of Cavalaire and the Îles d'Or, l'Androuno ~29 cm wide — Saint-Tropez Tourisme / Wikipedia (L'Androuno)

old.name: Ramatuelle
old.label: ~25–30 min
old.hook: A concentric hilltop village of vaulted passages and honey stone, ringed by the vineyards that climb toward Pampelonne.
old.text: A concentric hilltop village of vaulted passages and honey stone, ringed by the vineyards that climb toward Pampelonne. Its Théâtre de Verdure hosts the jazz and theatre festivals; below it lie the biodynamic estates (Fondugues-Pradugues) and the AOC Côtes de Provence vines of the peninsula.

old.name: Bormes-les-Mimosas
old.label: ~35 min west
old.hook: A cascading flowered old town above the sea, famous for its mimosa, which erupts yellow from January to March across some 90 species.
old.text: A cascading flowered old town above the sea, famous for its mimosa, which erupts yellow from January to March across some 90 species. Newly classed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France (label awarded September 2024); a microclimate lets hundreds of plant species grow through its cobbled lanes — effectively an open-air garden village.

old.name: Collobrières & the Chartreuse de la Verne
old.label: ~40 min inland, into the Massif des Maures
old.hook: The chestnut capital of the Maures (come for marrons glacés and chestnut cream), paired with a lonely 12th-century Carthusian monastery deep in the cork-oak forest.
old.text: The chestnut capital of the Maures (come for marrons glacés and chestnut cream), paired with a lonely 12th-century Carthusian monastery deep in the cork-oak forest. The Chartreuse de la Verne (founded 1170), restored in the Maures' green serpentine stone, has since 1983 sheltered a silent community of the sisters of Bethlehem — the best-preserved charterhouse in Provence, reached by a forest road.

old.name: Îles d'Hyères — Porquerolles & Port-Cros
old.label: Day trip; seasonal ferry from Cavalaire/La Croix-Valmer (~May–Sept), year-round from Le Lavandou
old.hook: The 'Golden Islands': Porquerolles with white-sand beaches, vineyards and the Fondation Carmignac art villa; Port-Cros a car-free forested peak ringed by clear water.
old.text: The 'Golden Islands': Porquerolles with white-sand beaches, vineyards and the Fondation Carmignac art villa; Port-Cros a car-free forested peak ringed by clear water. Port-Cros became Europe's oldest marine national park in 1963; both are protected, so the crowds thin the moment you leave the village quay. Boats run with Vedettes Îles d'Or & Le Corsaire.
